name: Ruy Lopez, Closed Defence
note: The main line of the Spanish. White keeps the bishop, castles and prepares d4; Black's …b5 and …d6 make a solid wall.

name: Ruy Lopez, Closed, 9.h3
note: The same wall with 9.h3 stopping …Bg4 before d4. The starting point of the Chigorin, Breyer and Zaitsev systems.

name: Ruy Lopez, Open Defence
note: Black takes on e4 and fights for activity: a knight on e4 and free pieces against White's better structure.

name: Ruy Lopez, Berlin Defence
note: The Berlin Wall: queens come off on move eight. Black's doubled pawns and bishop pair against White's healthy majority.

name: Ruy Lopez, Exchange Variation
note: White gives the bishop pair for a better pawn structure and aims for an endgame where the kingside majority counts.

name: Italian Game, Giuoco Pianissimo
note: The slow Italian: c3 and d3, castle, then the knight tour to g3 and the d4 break. The system taught in this course.

name: Italian Game, Giuoco Piano, 5.d4
note: The old main line: White builds the full centre at once and accepts a pin on b4. The position opens early.

name: Two Knights Defence, 4.d3
note: Black plays …Nf6 before …Bc5 and White declines the sharp lines. It transposes to the slow Italian.

name: Two Knights Defence, 4.Ng5
note: The knight attacks f7 at once. Black gives a pawn with 5…Na5 and gets active play against the offside bishop.

name: Scotch Game, Classical 4…Bc5
note: White opens the centre on move three. Black hits the knight with bishop and queen; White answers with c3 and Bc4.

name: Scotch Game, Mieses Variation
note: Black takes on c6 with the b-pawn and after e5 the knight goes to d5. Unbalanced pawns for both sides.

name: Petrov Defence, Classical
note: Black copies the knight move and, after 3…d6 first, takes on e4 safely. Symmetrical and solid.

name: Petrov Defence, 3.d4
note: White strikes in the centre instead of taking on e5. Pieces come off quickly; a common way to avoid the main Petrov.

name: Vienna Game
note: 2.Nc3 keeps f4 in reserve. With Bc4 and d3 it is an Italian with a King's Gambit idea in the pocket.

name: Four Knights, Spanish Variation
note: All four knights out by move three. Black mirrors with …Bb4 and a quiet, balanced game follows.

name: Philidor Defence
note: Black supports e5 with the d-pawn. Solid but passive; the bishop on f8 needs a plan.

name: Najdorf, English Attack
note: Be3, f3 and Qd2, then castle long and push g4. The most feared setup against the Najdorf.

name: Najdorf, 6.Be2
note: The classical, positional treatment: castle short and play for d5 rather than a pawn storm.

name: Dragon, Yugoslav Attack
note: Opposite-side castling and a race: White pushes h4–h5, Black storms the queenside. The sharpest opening in chess.

name: Sveshnikov
note: Black accepts a hole on d5 and a backward d6 pawn for active pieces and the bishop pair.

name: Accelerated Dragon
note: The fianchetto without …d6, so …d5 can come in one move. White's best answer is the Maroczy bind with c4.

name: Taimanov
note: Flexible: …e6, …Nc6 and …Qc7, keeping every option open. White usually castles long.

name: Kan
note: …e6 and …a6 with a small centre. White's most common reply is a Maroczy setup with c4.

name: Moscow Variation, 3.Bb5+
note: The check trades bishops early and sidesteps open-Sicilian theory. Calm, with a small edge in space.

name: Rossolimo Variation
note: 3.Bb5 against …Nc6. White may double Black's pawns or simply develop; a favourite at the top.

name: Closed Sicilian
note: White fianchettoes and plays f4: a kingside attack without opening the centre.

name: Alapin, 2…Nf6
note: 2.c3 prepares d4 with a pawn. Black's knight harasses e5 and the game resembles an Advance French.

name: Alapin, 2…d5
note: Black takes the centre pawn and brings the queen out early; White gains tempi but Black's structure is sound.

name: Winawer, Poisoned Pawn
note: White takes on g7 with the queen; Black gets the centre and open lines. Wild and deeply analysed.

name: Classical, 4.Bg5
note: Black keeps the bishop with …Be7 and after e5 trades it on e7. A closed centre and long plans.

name: Tarrasch, 3…c5
note: Black opens the position at once; an isolated d-pawn often results, with active pieces to compensate.

name: Tarrasch, 3…Nf6
note: The closed centre: White's e5 pawn against Black's …c5 and …f6 breaks.

name: Advance Variation
note: White fixes the pawn on e5 and defends d4. Black attacks it with …c5, …Nc6 and …Qb6.

name: Exchange Variation
note: Symmetrical pawns give an open, easy game. Drawish only if both sides want it to be.

name: Classical, 4…Bf5
note: The bishop escapes to f5, is chased with h4–h5 and traded on d3. The reference line of this course.

name: Tartakower, 5…exf6
note: Black recaptures on f6 with the e-pawn, opening the f-file and keeping a compact structure.

name: Advance, Short System
note: White develops calmly with Nf3 and Be2 and keeps the space from e5. Quiet and modern.

name: Advance, 4.Nc3 and g4
note: White pushes g4 to harass the bishop. Sharp: both kings stay in the centre for a while.

name: Exchange Variation
note: Symmetrical pawns; White's Bd3 and Bf4 aim at a slow kingside attack.

name: Panov Attack
note: c4 gives White an isolated d-pawn with open lines and activity. Nothing like the usual Caro-Kann.

name: Two Knights Variation
note: White develops both knights and delays d4. Black trades the bishop on f3 for a solid setup.

name: Pirc Defence, Classical
note: Black fianchettoes and waits. White builds a full centre and plays a4 and h3 to restrict counterplay.

name: Pirc Defence, Austrian Attack
note: f4 grabs space and prepares e5. Black must counter quickly in the centre.

name: Scandinavian, 3…Qa5
note: The queen comes out on move two and sits on a5. Easy to learn, solid, slightly passive.

name: Scandinavian, 2…Nf6
note: Black delays recapturing and develops first. The knight on d5 and bishop on g4 give a comfortable game.

name: Alekhine's Defence, Modern
note: Black invites e5 and hopes to attack the advanced pawns. 4.Nf3 keeps the centre under control.

name: QGD Orthodox, Capablanca's manoeuvre
note: Black waits for Bd3, takes on c4 and plays …Nd5 to trade pieces and free the position.

name: QGD Exchange Variation
note: White trades on d5 and attacks c6 with b4–b5, the minority attack. Black aims for …Ne4 and a kingside attack.

name: QGD, Harrwitz Attack 5.Bf4
note: The bishop goes to f4 and Black frees the position with …c5 at once.

name: Slav Defence, main line
note: …c6 keeps the bishop free; after …dxc4 and 5.a4 Bf5 Black develops it before …e6.

name: Slav, 4.e3 Bf5
note: White avoids the main theory and later trades the bishop with Nh4.

name: Semi-Slav, Meran
note: Black takes on c4 and pushes …b5. A dynamic queenside majority against White's centre.

name: Queen's Gambit Accepted, Classical
note: Black takes the pawn, gives it back, and plays …c5 for a free game.

name: Queen's Gambit Accepted, 3.e4
note: White takes the whole centre; Black hits it with …Nf6 and …e5 or …c5.

name: Tarrasch Defence
note: Black accepts an isolated d-pawn for active pieces. White fianchettoes to press it.

name: Colle System
note: d4, e3, Bd3, c3 and Nbd2, then e4. A quiet setup with a Greek gift waiting on h7.

name: London System, 2.Nf3 and 3.Bf4
note: The London with Nf3 first, avoiding early …c5 tricks.

name: London System, 2.Bf4
note: The direct London. Same pyramid, bishop outside it first. The system taught in this course.

name: Nimzo-Indian, Rubinstein 4.e3
note: 4.e3 keeps everything flexible. Black pins the knight and plays …d5 and …c5.

name: Nimzo-Indian, Classical 4.Qc2
note: White avoids doubled pawns; Black takes on c3 and plays …b6, …Bb7 and …d6.

name: Queen's Indian, 4.g3 Ba6
note: The bishop attacks c4 from a6 instead of b7, making White defend the pawn awkwardly.

name: QGD, Lasker Defence
note: …h6, …Ne4 and trades on e4 and e7. Simplifies early; a favourite equaliser.

name: King's Indian, Mar del Plata
note: The classic race: Black's …f5 pawn storm against White's c5 and b4 on the other wing.

name: King's Indian, Sämisch
note: f3 supports e4 and prepares Be3, Qd2 and castling long. Black counters with …e5 and …Nh5.

name: King's Indian, Makogonov 6.h3
note: 6.h3 keeps …Bg4 out and prepares g4. A modern, slow-burning treatment.

name: Grünfeld, Exchange Variation
note: Black gives up the centre and attacks it with …c5 and the g7 bishop. White's big centre against Black's pieces.

name: King's Indian, Fianchetto
note: White mirrors the fianchetto. Slower and safer; the fight is about the e5 and c5 breaks.

name: Modern Benoni
note: Black gets a queenside majority and the long diagonal; White gets the centre and e5 ideas.

name: Benko Gambit
note: A pawn for two open files on the queenside and lasting pressure that survives into the endgame.

name: London vs the Queen's Indian setup
note: The London against …e6 and …b6: Bd3, castle, then the e4 break or a knight to e5.

name: London vs the King's Indian setup
note: The London against …g6: h3 keeps the bishop safe, Be2 and castling, then c3 and Ne5.

name: Dutch Defence, Leningrad
note: …f5 with a fianchetto: Black wants …e5 and a kingside attack. White plays d5 and Rb1–b4.

name: Philidor, Hanham setup
note: A modern move order into the Philidor: solid, with …e5 held by …Nbd7 and …c6.

name: English, Reversed Dragon
note: 1.c4 e5 with g3: a Sicilian Dragon with colours reversed and an extra tempo.

name: English, Botvinnik setup
note: c4, g3, e4 and d3 against …Nc6 and …g6. A closed, manoeuvring game.

name: English, Symmetrical, 3…d5
note: The …d5 break; after e4 the knight goes to b4 and play on the c-file begins.

name: English, Symmetrical, 3.d4
note: Transposes toward Sicilian structures with c4 already in: a Maroczy-like bind for White.

name: QGD Tartakower (via 1.c4)
note: Fischer–Spassky, game 6. …b6 and …Bb7 solve the bishop problem; White trades on d5 and presses.

name: English vs the King's Indian setup
note: Both sides fianchetto; White holds back d4 and plays on the queenside with b4.

name: King's Indian Attack
note: White plays the King's Indian with an extra tempo: Nf3, g3, Bg2, d3, e4 and a kingside attack.

name: QGD, Harrwitz Attack (via 1.Nf3)
note: The 5.Bf4 line reached through 1.Nf3. Same plans as the direct move order.

name: King's Indian, Mar del Plata (via 1.Nf3)
note: The same Mar del Plata race reached through 1.Nf3 Nf6 2.c4 g6.

name: English, Symmetrical, Rubinstein
note: …d5 and …Nc7 aiming for …e5: Black takes the centre in the symmetrical English.

name: Nimzo-Larsen Attack
note: 1.b3 puts the bishop on the long diagonal first. Unusual, sound, and good for surprise.
